"Does everyone understand?" is a weak comprehension check mainly because it: (Apply) a) takes too long b) cannot be asked of a large class c) is too informal d) samples c
The claim that learners follow the non-verbal channel when the two contradict is best described as: (Understand) a) an established finding of the studies cited in this un

Explain why summing the components of effectiveness into a single score is a worse instrument than holding them separately. (Analyze)

List five non-verbal channels and give the classroom use of each. (Remember)
Explain the difference between a teacher who tries new methods and a teacher exercising the researcher role. (Understand)
Explain why a newly qualified teacher who criticises established practice is not thereby a change agent, and state what would have to come first. (Analyze)

"The five evolving roles are unrealistic for a teacher in a Pakistani government school with sixty pupils in a class and no resources." Evaluate this claim. Your answer m
c - narrowing to the test raises measured attainment while reducing the breadth of what was learned.
a - contribution to colleagues sits outside classroom processes; the other three are within.
b - attitude is read from ordinary conduct, which is why it cannot be asserted.
d - the excess of empathy is excusing, which communicates lowered expectation.
a - the relationship is instrumental in both directions: action at home, and information the classroom cannot supply.
c - dignity, and the practical impossibility of retreating in front of an audience.
d - it samples confidence, and the pupils who answer are the ones who least need checking.
b - worth acting on, and not established by the sources cited here; discarding the number while keeping its conclusion would be the same citation failure. (c) overstates:
a - the advance decision about evidence and the comparison are what make it research.
d - cumulative; a teacher who cannot explain has skipped transmission, not surpassed it.
